name: Chemical kinetics rate laws and reaction mechanisms

questions.q: What is defined as the rate of a chemical reaction at any specific instant in time?
a: The change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit time, determined from the gradient of a concentration-time graph
The total time taken for a reaction to reach completion
The initial concentration of reactants divided by total volume
The activation energy divided by temperature

questions.q: What does the order of a reaction with respect to a specific reactant represent in a rate equation?
a: The stoichiometric coefficient of that reactant in the balanced equation
The power to which the concentration of that reactant is raised in the experimentally determined rate equation
The number of moles of reactant consumed per second
The activation energy barrier for that reactant

questions.q: What is the overall order of a chemical reaction whose rate equation is given by Rate = k [A]<sup>2</sup> [B]<sup>1</sup>?
a: First order
Second order
Third order
Zero order

questions.q: How does the half-life of a first-order reactant depend on its initial concentration?
a: Half-life increases as initial concentration increases
Half-life decreases as initial concentration increases
Half-life is directly proportional to concentration squared
Half-life is constant and independent of the initial concentration

questions.q: What is the units of the rate constant (k) for a second-order overall reaction where rate has units of mol dm<sup>-3</sup> s<sup>-1</sup> and concentration has units of mol dm<sup>-3</sup>?
a: dm<sup>3</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>
s<sup>-1</sup>
mol dm<sup>-3</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>
dm<sup>6</sup> mol<sup>-2</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>

questions.q: According to the Arrhenius equation, what effect does an increase in temperature have on the rate constant (k) of a chemical reaction?
a: The rate constant decreases exponentially
The rate constant increases exponentially because more molecules exceed the activation energy
The rate constant remains completely unchanged
The rate constant becomes zero

questions.q: What is the role of a catalyst in a chemical reaction mechanism?
a: It is consumed permanently to form products
It shifts the position of chemical equilibrium to the right
It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy, increasing reaction rate without being used up
It increases the enthalpy change of the reaction

questions.q: What term describes the slowest step in a multi-step reaction mechanism that determines the overall rate of the reaction?
a: Fast equilibrium step
Termination step
Initiation step
Rate-determining step

questions.q: What is indicated by a zero-order reaction with respect to a reactant?
a: Changing the concentration of that reactant has no effect on the rate of the reaction
The reactant is completely absent from the reaction mixture
The reaction rate is infinite
The half-life of the reactant decreases over time

questions.q: What experimental method can be used to monitor the rate of a reaction that produces a gas?
a: Measuring electrical conductivity changes over time
Measuring volume of gas evolved using a gas syringe or mass loss on a balance
Titrating aliquots with acid-base indicators
Measuring refractive index changes

questions.q: Which of the following parameters can be determined graphically from a plot of ln(k) versus 1/T according to the linear Arrhenius equation?
a: Activation energy from the y-intercept
Enthalpy change of reaction from the curve
Activation energy from the gradient and the pre-exponential factor from the intercept
Rate constant directly at zero Kelvin

questions.q: What is the defining characteristic of a homogeneous catalyst in a reaction system?
a: It exists in a different physical state from the reactants
It is a solid mesh suspended in a liquid solution
It is destroyed during the first step of the mechanism
It exists in the same physical phase as the reactants (e.g., all in aqueous solution or all gases)

questions.q: How does an increase in reactant concentration affect the rate of a chemical reaction according to collision theory?
a: Frequency of effective collisions between reactant particles increases, thereby increasing the reaction rate
Kinetic energy of individual particles increases
Activation energy of the reaction decreases
Number of intermediate steps increases

questions.q: What is a reaction intermediate in a multi-step reaction mechanism?
a: The final stable product of the reaction
A species formed in one step of a mechanism and consumed in a subsequent step, which does not appear in the overall balanced equation
The initial reactant added to the flask
A homogeneous catalyst

questions.q: Which of the following statements about heterogeneous catalysis is correct?
a: The catalyst is in the same phase as the reactants
Heterogeneous catalysts do not involve adsorption of reactants onto active sites
The catalyst is in a different phase (typically a solid catalyst interacting with gaseous or liquid reactants)
Heterogeneous catalysts lower reaction enthalpy

questions.q: What is the molecularity of an elementary reaction step where three reactant particles collide simultaneously?
a: Unimolecular
Bimolecular
Tetramolecular
Termolecular

questions.q: If a reaction is first order with respect to reactant X, what happens to the initial rate if the concentration of X is tripled?
a: The rate increases by a factor of 3
The rate increases by a factor of 9
The rate remains unchanged
The rate decreases by a factor of 3

questions.q: What is measured during an iodine clock experiment to determine initial reaction rates?
a: The exact temperature of the vessel
The time taken for a sudden color change or appearance of a blue-black starch-iodine complex to occur
The total mass of iodine crystals added
The electrical potential of the solution

questions.q: Why does a rise in temperature increase the rate of a chemical reaction significantly more than predicted by the slight increase in collision frequency?
a: Molecules become heavier at higher temperatures
The volume of the container expands
A large proportion of reactant molecules gain kinetic energy equal to or exceeding the activation energy (E_a), drastically increasing successful collision frequency
Catalysts become more active

questions.q: What is the overall order of a reaction whose rate law is Rate = k [A]<sup>0</sup>?
a: First order
Second order
Fractional order
Zero order

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the activation energy of a catalyzed reaction compared to the uncatalyzed pathway?
a: Lower activation energy
Higher activation energy
Equal activation energy
Negative activation energy

questions.q: How is the order of reaction with respect to a reactant determined experimentally using initial rates data?
a: By measuring the final equilibrium yield
By comparing how changes in the initial concentration of that reactant affect the initial rate of the reaction while keeping other concentrations constant
By calculating standard enthalpy of formation
By measuring pH changes at room temperature

questions.q: What is indicated if the half-life of a reactant increases progressively as the reaction proceeds?
a: The reaction is first order
The reaction is zero order
The reaction is second order with respect to that reactant
The reaction has reached chemical equilibrium

questions.q: What does the term 'molecularity' refer to in chemical kinetics?
a: The total number of moles of products formed
The concentration of solute in moles per decimeter cubed
The total number of reactant molecules or ions taking part in an overall stoichiometric equation
The number of individual reactant particles (molecules, atoms, or ions) colliding together in an elementary reaction step

questions.q: Which of the following graph types yields a straight line for a zero-order reaction?
a: Concentration versus time
Rate versus concentration squared
Natural logarithm of concentration versus time
Reciprocal concentration versus time

questions.q: What physical property change is monitored using a spectrophotometer or colorimeter to study the kinetics of a colored reaction mixture?
a: Electrical conductivity
Light absorption (absorbance) proportional to concentration
Gas pressure in a sealed vessel
Mass loss on an analytical balance

questions.q: If the rate equation for a reaction is Rate = k [A] [B], and the concentration of both A and B are doubled, by what factor does the reaction rate increase?
a: Factor of 2
Factor of 3
Factor of 4
Factor of 8

questions.q: What is the primary function of catalytic converters fitted to automobile exhaust systems?
a: To convert carbon dioxide into oxygen gas
To store excess fuel during acceleration
To filter out soot particles using paper membranes
To catalyze redox reactions converting toxic carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides into harmless nitrogen and carbon dioxide

questions.q: What is the unit of the rate constant (k) for a first-order overall reaction?
a: s<sup>-1</sup>
mol dm<sup>-3</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>
dm<sup>3</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>
dm<sup>6</sup> mol<sup>-2</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes how enzymes act as biological catalysts?
a: They operate effectively at any extreme temperature or pH level
They feature specific active sites that bind substrates, providing an alternative low-activation-energy pathway
They permanently bond to the products of the reaction
They shift equilibrium positions to favor 100 percent product yield

questions.q: What is deduced about a reaction mechanism if the rate equation includes a particular reactant, and that reactant appears in the rate-determining step?
a: The reactant must be a spectator ion
The reactant does not affect the speed of the reaction
The reactant (or species derived from it) is involved in or prior to the rate-determining step
The reaction must be zero order overall

questions.q: What does the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curve illustrate regarding molecular energies in a gas sample?
a: The exact position of every molecule in space
The molecular weights of isotopes
The proportion of reactant molecules that are solid versus liquid
The distribution of molecular kinetic energies at a given temperature, highlighting the fraction exceeding the activation energy
